clue.text: Bloomer concealed by old Roman Catholic

parts.note: hid is the past tense of hide, so it means concealed

explanation.surface: Something embarrassing hidden away by an elderly churchgoer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' suggests a blunder or old-fashioned underwear, but here it is simply something that blooms. The pieces run in answer order: old, Roman Catholic, then concealed.
explanation.definitionFit: A flowering plant can be called a bloomer, and this exotic plant is prized for its flowers.

clue.text: Totally dismissed just claim

parts.note: a batsman dismissed in cricket is out
a right is a just claim or entitlement

explanation.surface: A legitimate claim thrown out completely.
explanation.definitionFit: Completely or wholly is the adverbial sense, as in winning a contest without qualification.

clue.text: Charlie with last of sticky sweets

parts.note: Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet
and means together with

indicators.note: last of says the final letter of sticky is taken

explanation.surface: A child called Charlie with the remains of some sticky sweets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is not a link here; it gives AND.
explanation.definitionFit: In American English this word covers confectionery in general, what Britons call sweets.

clue.text: I was introduced to American after seizing power

indicators.note: seizing says the string of pieces before it grabs the power letter and holds it inside

parts.note: met means was introduced to, as in we met at a party
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: Someone recalls meeting an American after a coup in which power was grabbed.
explanation.walkthrough: As printed the clue lacks a separate definition: 'power' must do double duty, giving P and also defining the answer, a slip the Big Dave blogger flagged on the day.
explanation.definitionFit: Driving force or momentum behind an action is a kind of power that keeps something moving.

clue.text: Sly character in western given help by lawman, at first

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for west or western
to ease is to help or relieve

indicators.note: at first tells us to take only the opening letter of lawman

explanation.surface: In a cowboy film, a shifty villain gets assistance from the sheriff.
explanation.definitionFit: This small cunning carnivore lends its name to a sneaky, untrustworthy person.

clue.text: Tag one article in English gym

indicators.note: in places the one-and-article letters inside the English-gym letters

parts.note: PT, physical training, is school gym
I is the Roman numeral one
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: A label attached to an item of English sportswear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gym' is PT, physical training, not PE.
explanation.definitionFit: A descriptive nickname or label attached to someone, like 'the Great', is a tag.

clue.text: One may help one escape from a trap

definitions.text: One may help one escape from a trap

parts.words: One may help one escape from a trap
parts.note: the trap is a golf bunker, and this lofted iron is the club used to get out of one

explanation.surface: Something that helps a person get free from a snare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trap' is golf slang for a sand bunker, and a particular club is designed to splash the ball out.
explanation.definitionFit: This lofted golf club is designed for playing out of bunkers, which are also called sand traps.

clue.text: Fire escape

definitions.meaning: to discharge a gun or firework
a narrow avoidance of punishment or harm

explanation.surface: A metal stairway on the outside of a building.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the phrase means discharge, as with fireworks; as a noun it means a lucky reprieve.

clue.text: Keep cards in rack each year close to Lent

parts.note: a rack is a stand for holding things
PA is short for per annum, Latin for each year

indicators.note: close to means the closing letter of the word Lent is taken

explanation.surface: Someone keeps greeting cards on a rack every year until the end of Lent.
explanation.walkthrough: In poker, to stand pat is to keep the hand you were dealt and draw no new cards.
explanation.definitionFit: A poker player who declines to exchange any of the dealt hand holds on to those cards.

clue.text: Insensitive, albeit not as much following start of talks

indicators.note: following places the not-as-much word after the opening letter of talks

parts.note: albeit and though both mean even if

indicators.note: start of says the opening letter of talks is taken

parts.note: less means not as much

explanation.surface: A remark about someone being tactless, though less so once the talks began.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who does not consider other people's feelings is inconsiderate or tactless.

clue.text: Set fire to fuel left out

indicators.note: out says the letter for left is removed from the fuel word

parts.note: lignite is brown coal, a low-grade fuel

explanation.surface: An instruction to burn fuel that has been left lying around outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left out' reads as one phrase meaning abandoned, but 'left' gives L and 'out' tells you to remove it from LIGNITE.
explanation.definitionFit: To kindle something is to make it start burning, a direct synonym of setting it alight.

clue.text: Minute part of it in yolk

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A tiny fleck of something inside an egg yolk.
explanation.definitionFit: Minute, pronounced my-NEWT, is an adjective meaning extremely small.

clue.text: Dutch after cup, status symbol

indicators.note: after places the spouse word behind the prize word

parts.note: a cup awarded as a prize is a trophy
'my old Dutch' is cockney slang for a man's spouse, from Duchess of Fife

explanation.surface: A Dutch footballer, having won the cup, becomes a celebrity status symbol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dutch' is not the nationality: in cockney rhyming slang 'Dutch' (Duchess of Fife) means a man's wife.
explanation.definitionFit: A young glamorous spouse displayed by a wealthy man is treated as an emblem of his success.

clue.text: Got shirt messy in outhouse, like Billy Bunter?

indicators.note: in places the jumbled letters inside the outbuilding word

parts.note: a shed is an outhouse

indicators.note: messy says the letters of got shirt are jumbled

explanation.surface: A boy's shirt got dirty in the garden shed, as a schoolboy character might manage.
explanation.walkthrough: Billy Bunter, the fat schoolboy of Frank Richards' Greyfriars stories, wore thick spectacles. 'messy' signals the anagram of GOT SHIRT and 'in' places it within the outhouse.
explanation.definitionFit: Bunter's thick round glasses mark him as someone who cannot see distant things clearly.

clue.text: Storyteller in court, near to collapse

indicators.note: to collapse suggests the letters of court and near fall into a new order

explanation.surface: A narrator in a courtroom, close to breaking down.
explanation.definitionFit: This French borrowing names a person skilled at telling anecdotes entertainingly.

clue.text: Highest score is excellent

parts.note: top means highest
to score is to cut a notch, a mark used to keep a tally

explanation.surface: Getting the highest mark is a sign of outstanding work.
explanation.definitionFit: First-rate or of the highest quality is the informal sense of the hyphenated phrase.

clue.text: Singer's bar number, by Otis Redding initially

definitions.note: read as 'Singer is', so the definition is the singer and the 's is a link

parts.note: the counter is the bar in a pub
ten is a number

indicators.note: initially tells us to take the opening letters of Otis and Redding

explanation.surface: A soul singer performs a numbered song in a bar, an Otis Redding cover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Singer's' stands for 'Singer is', the 's being a link to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A male vocalist singing in the alto range above tenor is a kind of singer.

clue.text: Better ahead overlooking station

indicators.note: overlooking places the ahead word above the rank word in this down entry

parts.note: up means ahead, as in being one up
station means rank or grade in life

explanation.surface: A better position ahead, with a view over a railway station.
explanation.definitionFit: To improve something is to raise it to a higher standard, as a verb meaning make better.

clue.text: Resume painting to support others

indicators.note: to support places the painting word underneath the others word in this down entry

parts.note: the rest are the others
painting is a form of art

explanation.surface: Taking up painting again to help other people.
explanation.definitionFit: To begin again after a pause is to recommence, so both verbs share the sense.

clue.text: Spectre of international consumed by anger

indicators.note: consumed by puts the international letter inside the anger word

parts.note: wrath is great anger

explanation.surface: The ghost of a sportsman capped internationally, eaten up by rage.
explanation.definitionFit: A ghost or apparition, especially of someone seen just before their death, is a spectre.

clue.text: Offend stranger playing with small son

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters of stranger are moved about

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
S is the abbreviation for son in genealogies

explanation.surface: Someone causes offence by a stranger playing with their little boy.
explanation.definitionFit: To break a rule or moral law is to commit an offence, so the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Report made by knight during case

indicators.note: during puts the knight letter in the middle of the case word

parts.note: a bag is a case for carrying things
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: A dispatch written by a knight while a legal case is underway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Report' is not a document but the sound of a gun firing.
explanation.definitionFit: A report is a loud explosive noise such as a gunshot, the sense used here.

clue.text: Meat company breaking embargo

indicators.note: breaking says the company letters split the embargo word

parts.note: a ban is an embargo

explanation.surface: A meat firm defying a trade embargo.
explanation.definitionFit: Cured pork from the back or sides of a pig is a type of meat.

clue.text: Pictures of guys returning, arrested by US agents

indicators.note: arrested by puts the reversed men inside the agency letters

parts.note: the CIA is the American intelligence agency

indicators.note: returning means the word for guys is read backwards

parts.note: guys are men

explanation.surface: Photographs of men coming home who are detained by American agents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' reverses the guys and 'arrested by' places them inside the agency; 'Pictures' here means films, not photographs.
explanation.definitionFit: Going to the pictures is an informal British way of saying going to see a film.

clue.text: Want Mark to face Manchester, say

parts.note: a scar is a mark left on the skin
Manchester is an example of a city

explanation.surface: A footballer named Mark wants to play against Manchester's team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' poses as a name and 'Manchester' as a football club; 'to face' only means the scar comes first, and 'Want' is a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Want as a noun means lack or shortage, as in living in want.

clue.text: Large insect runs inside on the ground

indicators.note: inside places the runs letter within the rearranged letters
ground, as in ground up, says the letters of on the are crushed into a new order

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A big bug scurries indoors along the floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the ground' reads as a location, but 'ground' is the anagram signal for ON THE.
explanation.definitionFit: This stinging wasp is the largest of its family in Europe, hence a large insect.

clue.text: Awful smell coming from traps over by church

indicators.note: over means the word for traps is turned back to front

parts.note: nets are traps for catching fish or animals

explanation.surface: A foul odour wafting from animal traps beside a church.
explanation.definitionFit: A stink or foul odour is a synonym for an awful smell.
